Player's manual · version 0.10.3

AI Showdown

A parody 3D fighting game where eleven AI-industry caricatures and AGI itself settle the future in best-of-three bouts across four stages. One-button Power specials, cinematic Supers, and no motion inputs required.

Parody. Not affiliated with or endorsed by any real person or company. Built in Godot 4.7.2.

01Getting started

Download the build for your system, unpack it, and run it directly. There is no installer.

SystemArchiveHow to start
Windows 10/11 (64-bit)AIShowdown-v0.10.3-windows.zipExtract the entire zip and run AIShowdown.exe. If SmartScreen warns on an unsigned indie binary, click More info → Run anyway.
macOS 11+ (Apple Silicon & Intel)AIShowdown-v0.10.3-macos.zipUnzip and open AIShowdown.app. For local unsigned builds, Control-click the app → Open → Open, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
Linux (x86_64)AIShowdown-v0.10.3-linux.tar.gzExtract with tar xzf AIShowdown-v0.10.3-linux.tar.gz and run ./AIShowdown/AIShowdown.x86_64.

Note: The Online menu is hidden in this build (SHOW_ONLINE = false) because online/servers.json still points at the original 3D Fighter lobby server.

03Controls

AI Showdown uses a one-button special scheme so anyone can throw specials and Supers right away. Directions are relative to the screen ("forward" flips automatically when you switch sides).

ActionPlayer 1 keyboardGamepad
Move / jump / crouchW A S DLeft stick / D-pad
LP / HP Light / Heavy PunchU / IX / Y
LK / HK Light / Heavy KickJ / KA / B
Power Power specialOLB
Super Super movePRT
SS SidestepLRB
Pause & move listEscStart
  • Power specials: Press Power (O / LB) for your fighter's signature special; hold a direction (forward, back, or down) with Power for their other specials. Super (P / RT) triggers the cinematic Super once your meter is full. No motion inputs are needed; open the pause menu during a fight to view your fighter's move list.
  • Player 2: Uses the arrow keys with Num 4/5 (punches), Num 1/2 (kicks), Num 7/8 (Power/Super) and Num 6 (sidestep), or a second gamepad. On keyboards without a numpad, the fallback keys are [ ] (punches), ; ' (kicks), \ (Power), = (Super) and / (sidestep).
  • Remapping: Every key and gamepad button can be changed per player in Options → Controls. If you only have one gamepad, use Swap Pads in Options to assign it to Player 2.

04Fighting basics

Win two 99-second rounds to take a match (except 1v1 Quick Match, which is a single round). Lower the opponent's health bar to zero, or hold more health when the clock hits 0.

Movement

  • Walk & dash: Hold toward or away to walk; tap toward twice to dash in, or tap back twice to backdash out of pressure.
  • Jump & crouch: Hold Up (plus left/right) to jump over projectiles or close distance; hold Down to duck under high hits.
  • Sidestep (L / RB): Steps briefly into the background or foreground plane to evade linear attacks and fireballs.

Blocking & throws

Attack typeBlocked byWhat hits it
HighStanding back (or crouching back whiffs/blocks depending on move)Quick jabs, many standing pokes and projectiles
MidStanding back or crouching backMost standing attacks, dashes and specials
LowHolding down-back onlyLow kicks, sweeps and ground-skimming moves
OverheadHolding back while standing onlyJumping attacks, overhead smashes, Sundar's 404 Not Found

Throws: Press LP+LK together up close to throw a blocking opponent. Hold back + LP+LK for a back throw that switches sides. Press LP+LK just as you are thrown to break free.

Counters & stage edges

Landing a hit while your opponent is in the startup of an attack triggers a COUNTER hit with extra hitstun. Hitting an opponent into the stage boundary with a heavy blow can trigger a wall splat for a follow-up.

05The fight screen

Clean slanted HUD bars keep the arena readable at a glance.

HUD elementWhat it shows
Health barsPlayer 1 on the top-left, Player 2 on the top-right. Recent damage trails briefly in red as the bar drains.
Round timerCentered at top (99 seconds per round, flashing in the final 10 seconds).
Fighter name & round pipsEach round won lights a round indicator under the bar; two wins takes a standard match.
Super meterBottom corners. Builds as you attack, block, and take damage. Glows when full and carries over between rounds.
Controls hintShown automatically on your first fight of a session to remind you of attacks, Power and Super.

Action camera & intros

As a bout heats up with big hits or juggles, the camera dynamically swings closer to frame the impact. You can set Action Camera to Full, Subtle or Off in Options. Pre-fight intros feature fighter-specific lines and rival banter; press any attack button to skip, or disable intros in Options.

06Power specials & supers

No quarter-circles or dragon-punch motions required.

Power specials

  • Press Power (O / Num 7 / \ / LB) alone for your fighter's neutral signature special.
  • Hold Forward, Back, or Down while pressing Power to unleash their alternate specials (projectiles, anti-airs, stances, armour rushes, command grabs, or teleports depending on the fighter).
  • Several heavy or rush moves feature super armour, letting them absorb a hit without flinching. Counter-stances and reflect moves catch incoming blows or send projectiles back.

Super moves

When your Super meter is completely full, press Super (P / Num 8 / = / RT). The screen flashes and freezes briefly on a cut-in before unleashing your fighter's cinematic finisher, consuming the full meter.

Normal attacks can be chained or cancelled on hit into Power specials or a Super for big bursts of damage.

Rethemed from Rooftop

09Story, Arcade & Versus

Story

Choose any fighter to play their personal campaign: an opening intro, six bouts with pre-fight and post-win dialogue, a rival confrontation, the final showdown with AGI in the Senate Hearing Room, and a unique ending.

Arcade

Battle through a ladder of CPU opponents ending with AGI in the Senate Hearing Room. If you play as AGI yourself, you face your own shadow in the final match. High scores are saved per fighter under Best Scores.

Vs CPU & 1v1 Quick Match

Vs CPU lets you pick both fighters and the stage for a best-of-3 bout. 1v1 Quick Match drops you straight into a single-round bout against a random CPU opponent on a random stage. CPU difficulty (Easy, Normal, Hard) is set in Options.

Versus (2 Players)

Local head-to-head on one computer using shared keyboard controls or two gamepads. Both players can swap characters, adjust handicaps, or rematch directly after each set.

Demo

Watches two CPU fighters duel on a random stage with no knockout timer. Press any button to return to the main menu.

10Training

Test moves, check frame advantage, practice punishes, and inspect hitboxes without round timers or K.O.s.

Press Tab (or Back on a gamepad) to open the Training menu.

Setting / ShortcutWhat it does
DummyStand, Crouch, Jump, CPU (fights back), or Playback (repeats recorded moves).
GuardNone, Block All, Block After First Hit, or Random.
Health Refill / Infinite MeterAutomatically restores health after combos or keeps Super meter filled.
Frame Data / Input History / HitboxesDisplays live startup/active/recovery/advantage numbers, recent inputs, or attack/body boxes.
Record / Playback (F6 / F7)Take control of the dummy with F6 to record up to 10 seconds of actions, then toggle playback with F7.
Reset positions (Backspace / L3)Returns both fighters to center stage immediately.

Note: Legacy combo trials are currently being removed from Training for AI Showdown's one-button move set.

AI Showdown simulates matches deterministically, saving lightweight input logs for up to 30 recent bouts (plus any replays you mark to Keep).

Screen / ActionKeyboardGamepad

Pause / play (while watching)SpaceA

Back / forward 5 seconds← / →D-pad left / right

Replays only play back on the same game version they were recorded on.

12Options

Changes save automatically to your Godot user data directory.

OptionChoices
Audio slidersMusic, Effects, Announcer/Voice, and Stage Ambience volumes.
Action CameraFull, Subtle, or Off.
CPU DifficultyEasy, Normal, or Hard.
Fight IntrosShow or skip pre-match dialogue intros by default.
Display & ResolutionFullscreen, Borderless, Windowed (preset window sizes), Render Scale, and Graphics quality preset (auto-tuned on first launch).
Swap Pads & ControlsAssign a single pad to Player 2, or open per-player keyboard/gamepad remapping.

User data locations: %APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\AI Showdown\ (Windows), ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/AI Showdown/ (macOS), and ~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/AI Showdown/ (Linux).

13Troubleshooting

  • Game won't start or shows black screen: AI Showdown uses Godot 4.7.2 Forward+ (Vulkan on Windows/Linux, Metal on macOS). Update your GPU drivers, or check that your GPU supports Vulkan 1.2+.
  • Low frame rate on a laptop or Retina screen: Lower Resolution or Graphics in Options (auto-graphics also steps down automatically if a match drops below 42 fps).
  • Special moves or Super aren't triggering: Use the single Power button (O / LB, optionally held with Forward, Back, or Down) — no quarter-circle motions are used. Super (P / RT) requires a full Super meter.
  • macOS says app is from an unidentified developer: Control-click AIShowdown.app → Open → Open, or allow it under System Settings → Privacy & Security.
  • Gamepad not controlling Player 1: Check Swap Pads in Options, or remap buttons in Options → Controls.
